_description: TRIALS arm B: ontology-guided NEGATIVE SELECTION only, single factor. Identical to config/lc_trials_baseline.json except trials_mesh_tiered_negatives=true, which attaches the MeSH matcher and tiers the topic's own graded qrels pool by MeSH tree distance instead of sampling it uniformly. Sample-level ontology weighting stays OFF.
_why_this_differs_from_the_label_budget_: The earlier trials arms (low_random / low_ontology in trials_domain/label_budget_runner.py) drew negatives from the UNJUDGED corpus and discarded the graded pool entirely. That answers a different question — can an ontology replace relevance judgments — and it is not comparable to the career learning curve, which keeps all its graded negatives and only toggles whether the ontology guides selection. These two configs mirror the career design instead: subsample records across ALL grades proportionally, keep the graded negatives, and vary only ontology-guided tiering. The corpus-negative study remains a separate contribution with its own table.
_paired_with: config/lc_career_ontneg_only.json / lc_career_baseline.json — same single mechanism over ESCO instead of MeSH.
_comment_cache: Dedicated path. The shared default is content-hash keyed, so one file would mix career and trials vectors.
_comment_augmentation: Off: the career augmenter rewrites role/title text with career transformation rules, which would produce clinically meaningless text from a patient narrative. Both slots already carry a pre-serialized encoder_view.
_comment_the_factor: THE ONE THING THAT VARIES, here switched ON. The MeSH matcher is attached and the graded selector orders each topic's ineligible+not_relevant pool by MeSH set distance to the patient, drawing preferentially from the closest tercile under the same 0.2->0.6 curriculum the baseline uses. Note the tiers here reorder a pool of HUMAN-GRADED negatives; they do not introduce unjudged candidates, so the label budget is identical to the baseline's.
_comment_no_matcher: MeSH matcher IS attached in this arm, via BatchProcessor.set_ontology_matcher, and supplies both the tiering distance and the coarse branch_distance.
_comment_negatives: Negatives come from the topic's own graded qrels pool via TrialsNegativeSelector, subsampled with the positives so the label budget is honest. Global pooling is off because pooling across topics would defeat the per-topic graded pool.
_comment_curriculum: Grade-1 (ineligible) share of negatives, ramped across training. Identical in both arms so it cannot confound the contrast.
